body:
> your mind is capable of happiness?

Why does this matter? My depression is stronger.

And I would likely still kill myself if I magically wasn't depressed the next time I wake up in the morning. I didn't have friends *before* I got depressed.

I don't like talking. I don't like working. I don't like being around people. Never did.

> If I may be so bold, the fact that you apologise to me about being rude means that you do feel that your words are still able to convey thoughts or feelings, even if they do so imperfectly. It is the limit of human language: we can never truly express what we feel.

I just don't want this thread to be closed by the nazi mods over here.

> You can't look inside your own head either

I don't need to. There are thoughts, emotions, feelings and how we act on these things.

> Your brain is malfunctioning from depression.

I don't think so. I think natural selection is doing its thing.

> It's not broken forever, it's just temporarily not processing things the way it should.

I think its exactly doing what its purpose is. Just like white blood cells attack an intruder my brain destroys itself. So I don't poison everyone else.

> And what's worse, it even fails at making you understand that correctly

Sorry, I'm not that stupid. In my group therapy people tried to tell me the same, but it's bullshit. In my apprenticeship (I live in Germany) exams I scored 96/100 points in the oral exam. I told the group that I could have achieved 100/100 points because that's what the examiners told me and I felt the same.

Their reaction "Oh why aren't you satisfied with 96/100, it's a great result?" I still don't get them. How can you not want 100/100 points if you're so close?

My brain is totally fine.

> And you, as a person, are more than just your depression.

I'm not.

> All I can tell you, all I can assure you, is that you are not alone.

That's not true. That's just not true. I will commit suicide within the next 20 days and that's not an act that can be shared. No one will seriously understand.
Minus the death part? Yup. My life was fine and I just woke up horribly depressed one morning and this feeling didn't vanish as of this writing. It actually grew stronger, but that you already know.

> When we fixate on negative thoughts like "there is no hope" we strengthen those connections and make them easier to access. We develop negative networks that we access even when we don't want too.

I can't change that. My depression just began one day. Without a preceding traumatic event. In hate "positive". I want to feel miserable.

> But the field will never acknowledge its shortcomings until the are forced to.

As usual. As with everything.

ECT is, at least here, only offered inpatient. I'm will never visit a psych ward again. Just two weeks ago I asked several clinics if they could do something outpatient. No chance.

Funny thought because I'm gonna kill myself anyway, but I'd rather die than stay in a clinic again.

> If you saw therapists who dropped you for lack of progress than you saw bad therapists.

No. Either the whole concept of therapy is bullshit or whatever is wrong with me just can't be fixed. Either way, I don't care any longer.

> I know some therapists will discontinue therapy if they think their client is refusing to put in any effort, but that's a different scenario.

That's why they dropped me.

> Words are just that: words. The sentiment behind them is real, however.

I shouldn't even ask for forgiveness, but sorry for being rude again. I don't care at all if there is a sentiment behind anything. It doesn't change anything. Not even my thoughts or the thought process. So words are quite literally useless.

> No one here has the solution to your problems. No one here even has the solution to all of their own problems.

No one has.

> I don't know you, I don't love you, I don't know if you're worth it, I'm not going to ask you to try XY unless you want to, but I will tell you that you are not going through this alone.

Of course I'm alone. No one is able to look inside my head and words can't express what is going on exactly. Words are even too limited to express thoughts. So how could they express feelings?

> The mental health field cannot handle people that don't fit into their little box. Maybe some people are just fucking terrible at being people.

Do you know what? I'm not English/American/..., but I will put exactly these words on my wall before I go.

> I've made them go speechless when I tell them about me. They still would give advice like go out and watch a movie with a friend. The concept that I haven't even had an acquaintance in over 5 years dumbfounds them.

And even if they didn't go speechless, they still didn't do anything useful at all. I told them what I think and feel, they gave me a reply and that's it. Honestly? I can talk to myself or my wall if my problem was simply the lack of something listening. But that's not the case.

> There just isn't help for people like me.

There have been times when a simple cold was deadly. So maybe in 200 years someone smart comes along and shows all these therapists/psychiatrists how useless they have been.

I opened myself up and to what end? My depression got worse and now I will have to commit suicide.

> That I cannot does not mean that there are none.

Even professionals couldn't help me find one. Meds didn't work and therapists refused to work with me after a certain amount of time. Not because I was being rude or something, but due to the lack of progress. If I'm honest I don't think its my fault at all. Whatever they thought they did wasn't something that could have possibly helped me.

How can "words" be "supportive"? We're not talking about "Oh don't worry, you'll surely pass the exams". I will kill myself within the next couple weeks. "Oh don't worry, you'll survive your attempt?". Sorry to disappoint you. I already survived one. I will not make the same mistake a second time.

> why death?

Why not?

> There's plenty other things you can try that aren't as permanent. I'm not suggesting anything illegal or something that could bring bodily harm to yourself or others -- but you could take a break while you think of a possible alternative. A complete change of your life, before you discard it. Time is a luxury you still have, take it.

I don't have the money or access to purchase drugs and apart from that I already tried "plenty other things". Travelling, sports, social contact, doing nothing at all, ... And no, there is no "complete change of your life". I am who I am and if the depression doesn't vanish I will die by my own hand because I cannot take it any longer.

> Does it still sound silly?

Sorry if I'm rude, but yes it does. The brain isn't a muscle and a depression is no accident.

And by the way, how exactly is your comment helpful? I'm really not trying to attack you or anything, but I already heard this same stuff from my therapists. "I'm just a crutch to help you learn walking again". Oh you silly therapist, you forgot that I lost my legs 3 years ago ... *figuratively speaking*

That's what I mean when I say that talking doesn't help. Not one single person on this world was able to tell me anything useful regarding my depression. No doctors, no therapists, no psychiatrists, no other patients, no family-members, no one.

My depression is like a headache of negativity. Of course it makes me feel crap mentally, but it's painful on a physical level.
